chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Was Charlie Parker well read? His voice
summary: Parker could talk on any subject; Mingus thinks he raised his voice to seem refined.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. I didn't know him well. You did, but I never could tell -- if he felt like it, he could talk about classical music, about political stuff, but I don't know if he really cared about it. It was just kind of a put-on. Was he very intelligent?

He was very well read, he had to have been. I never checked him out, because I've never read myself. I know he could talk on any subject, any subject I wanted to talk about. And I was told he was very well read.
But his wife, Jan, said nobody knew Charlie Parker. (Inaudible) his voice changed.

I listened to how he was talking with (inaudible) was telling him, you're so well read. was talking much higher. When I heard (inaudible), how are you? He had a bass voice. So I know he made an effort to do that.
